title: Weekly Top Five Articles: The Moral Crises Americans Pretend Not to See
author: Anthony B. Bradley
summary: This roundup is unified by a single editorial thesis: the interior architecture of personhood is being thinned by cheap external substitutes. Five articles are synthesized — covering online sports betting addiction, AI substitution at universities, sex-discrimination law's drift from persons to proxies, purity culture's damage to trauma survivors, and partisan identity as pseudo-religion — with Bradley providing substantive interpretive commentary connecting each to a common theme of formation vs. outsourcing of conscience.
points: Bradley's framing: from the betting app to the chatbot, from the statistical proxy to the purity script to the partisan reflex, the trade is always the same — substance exchanged for shortcut, conscience for outsourcing, soul for system.

Article 1 (Bradley): Online sports gambling hijacks dopamine circuitry in men with underdeveloped moral formation; the bet is never about money but about anticipation — counterfeit transcendence for men starved of the genuine article.

Article 2 (Yingling): Elite students are voluntarily handing over homework, emails, gym routines, even texts to girls — wholesale substitution of machine output for the human acts that make a university a university.
Article 3 (Bachiochi/Greco): Sex-discrimination law drifted from protecting the qualified individual to a statistical parity regime, damaging the working-class women it was designed to defend.

Article 4 (Dolan/Coates/Meston): Purity culture exposure amplifies sexual shame in trauma survivors — a script imposed without formation cannot bear the weight of a real human life; it hands wounded believers a verdict rather than soul-care.

Article 5 (Dolan/Schwadel): Racial resentment strongly predicts political conservatism among white mainline Protestants and Catholics; among white evangelicals, conservatism is near-uniform regardless — partisan identity functioning as quasi-religious commitment.
Synthesis: 'What makes a life work, and worth living, is a self formed in love, tutored by conscience, anchored in transcendence, and released into mission.'
quotes: From the betting app to the chatbot, from the statistical proxy to the Christian purity script to the partisan reflex, the trade is the same. Substance is exchanged for shortcut, conscience for outsourcing, soul for system.
A mind that no longer thinks for itself does not gain anything in the trade. It simply stops being a mind.
What makes a life work, and worth living, is a self formed in love, tutored by conscience, anchored in transcendence, and released into mission.
